'''Temetrius Jamel "Ja" Morant'''<ref name=Woo>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/01/23/ja-morant-murray-state-racers |title=Ja Morant, Murray State's High-Flying Star, Is No Longer College Hoops's Best Kept Secret |first=Jeremy |last=Woo |publisher=''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' |date=January 23, 2019 |accessdate=January 24, 2019}}</ref> (born August 10, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State Racers]]. An [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] as a sophomore in 2019, he is widely considered one of the top prospects as a potential top-three pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]].

Born in [[Dalzell, South Carolina]] as the son of former basketball player Tee Morant, Ja Morant was lightly recruited by [[NCAA Division I]] programs and unranked by [[college recruiting|recruiting]] services despite earning All-State distinction at Crestwood High School in [[Sumter, South Carolina]]. He made an immediate impact at Murray State, earning first-team All-OVC honors as a freshman. Morant had a breakout sophomore season, which saw him win [[Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|OVC Player of the Year]] and [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball season assists leaders|lead the NCAA in assists]]. As a sophomore, he also became the first player in NCAA history to average at least 20 points and 10 assists per game in a single season.

==Early life and high school==
Morant was born in [[Dalzell, South Carolina]] to Tee and Jamie Morant.<ref name="bio">{{cite web |title=Ja Morant |url=https://goracers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7643 |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=December 24, 2018}}</ref><ref name="yahoo">{{cite web |title=Ja Morant |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaab/players/141675/ |publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]] |accessdate=November 24, 2018}}</ref> His father was a high school teammate of [[Ray Allen]] and played basketball for [[Claflin University]] before starting a professional career abroad.{{uncited|date=May 2019}} However, he ended his basketball career when Ja was born and became a [[barber]] instead.<ref name=Woo/><ref name="sandlin">{{cite web |last1=Sandlin |first1=Blake |title=From Tee to Ja: Morant finishing what his father started |url=http://thenews.org/2018/02/22/from-tee-to-ja-morant-finishing-what-his-father-started/ |website=The Murray State News |accessdate=December 24, 2018 |date=February 22, 2018}}</ref> Morant trained in his backyard with his father, who taught him step-back [[Jump shot (basketball)|jump shots]] and bought [[tractor]] tires for him to practice jumping with a soft landing.<ref name="sayers">{{cite web |last1=Sayers |first1=Justin |title=The best NBA prospect you've never heard of? Murray State's Ja Morant |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2019/01/29/murray-state-ja-morant-ground-despite-nba-draft-potential/2642806002/ |website=[[The Courier-Journal]] |accessdate=January 30, 2019 |date=January 29, 2019}}</ref> In his childhood, he often faced older opponents, telling his mother, "I'm not worried about the big kids."<ref name="greer">{{cite web |last1=Greer |first1=Jeff |title=Who’s Ja Morant? The Murray State star is quietly making a name for himself and will soon be in an NBA city near you |url=https://theathletic.com/722371/2018/12/20/whos-ja-morant-the-murray-state-star-is-quietly-making-a-name-for-himself-and-will-soon-be-in-an-nba-city-near-you/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |accessdate=January 30, 2019 |date=December 20, 2018}}</ref> Morant played in the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit with the South Carolina Hornets, a small grassroots team based in [[Columbia, South Carolina]]. For a single season, he was teammates with [[Zion Williamson]], who would become one of the top players in his class.<ref name="norlander">{{cite web |last1=Norlander |first1=Matt |title=Court Report: The real story of Ja Morant and Zion Williamson playing on the same AAU team |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/court-report-the-real-story-of-ja-morant-zion-williamson-playing-on-the-same-aau-team/ |publisher=[[CBS Sports]] |accessdate=January 30, 2019 |date=January 23, 2019}}</ref>

Morant attended Crestwood High School in [[Sumter, South Carolina]].<ref name=bio/> He grew from {{height|ft=5|in=9}} to {{height|ft=6|in=0}} in his first three years with the basketball team.<ref name=Woo/> Morant left as its all-time leading scorer, with 1,679 [[point (basketball)|points]] and set a career-high with 56 points against [[Sumter High School]].<ref name=bio/><ref name="aubrey">{{cite web |last1=Aubrey |first1=Will |title=Racer recruiting class ‘among 10 best’ |url=https://theracerinsider.com/2016/11/10/racer-recruiting-class-among-10-best/ |publisher=Racer Insider |accessdate=December 24, 2018 |date=November 10, 2016}}</ref> In his final two seasons for Crestwood, he averaged 27 points, 8 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 8 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] per game, earning South Carolina Class 3A All-State honors in both years. Morant also left high school as a three-time All-Region [[most valuable player|Most Valuable Player]] (MVP).<ref name=bio/> Morant could not [[slam dunk|dunk]] until he was a senior.<ref name=sayers/>

===Recruiting===
Morant was not ranked by [[College recruiting|recruiting]] services [[ESPN]], [[247Sports.com|247Sports]], or [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].<ref name="rivals">{{cite web |title=Ja Morant |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2017/ja-morant-233377 |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |accessdate=December 26, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=J.A. Morant |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/225039/ja-morant |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=December 26, 2018}}</ref><ref name="247sports">{{cite web |title=Temetrius Morant |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Temetrius-Morant-46035335/high-school-183728/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=December 26, 2018}}</ref> His only high major [[NCAA Division I]] offer came from [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]].<ref name="hoy">{{cite web |last1=Hoy |first1=Jackson |title=2019 Draft Primer: Ja Morant, The Ultimate Sleeper |url=https://www.thestepien.com/2018/06/29/2019-draft-primer-ja-morant-the-ultimate-sleeper/ |publisher=The Stepien |accessdate=December 24, 2018 |date=June 29, 2018}}</ref> He was accidentally discovered by [[mid-major]] program [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]] of the [[Ohio Valley Conference]] (OVC) in July 2016, when assistant coach James Kane attended a camp hoping to see a player who was joining his team. While looking for a snack, Kane noticed Morant playing a [[3x3 basketball|three-on-three game]] in an auxiliary gym; impressed, he contacted head coach [[Matt McMahon (basketball)|Matt McMahon]], who soon offered Morant a [[Athletic scholarship|scholarship]].<ref name="dortch">{{cite web |last1=Dortch |first1=Chris |title=Once a little-known prospect, Morant has everyone's attention now |url=http://www.nba.com/article/2019/01/25/murray-state-ja-morant-diamond-rough |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |accessdate=January 28, 2019 |date=January 25, 2019}}</ref> On September 3, 2016, Morant committed to playing for Murray State during dinner at McMahon's house.<ref name=Woo/><ref name=sandlin/><ref name="byerly">{{cite web |last1=Byerly |first1=Justin |title=Future Racer: Ja Morant |url=https://www.prephoops.com/2017/02/future-racer-ja-morant/ |publisher=Prep Hoops |accessdate=December 24, 2018 |date=February 16, 2017}}</ref> His father said, "Every parent wants their child to play at a big-time program, but what I realized is, don't go where you want to be, go to where they want you."<ref name=Woo/> His other Division I offers included [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]], [[Maryland Eastern Shore Hawks men's basketball|Maryland Eastern Shore]], [[South Carolina State Bulldogs men's basketball|South Carolina State]], and [[Wofford Terriers men's basketball|Wofford]].<ref name=byerly/>

==College career==
=== Freshman year ===
On November 10, 2017, Morant debuted for Murray State with 7 points and a team-high 11 assists in a 118–61 victory over [[Brescia University]] of the [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics]] (NAIA).<ref>{{cite web |title=Racers Lockdown Brescia - Hawkins On Fire With 28 Points |url=https://goracers.com/news/2017/11/10/mens-basketball-murray-state-vs-brescia.aspx |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=March 24, 2019 |date=November 10, 2017}}</ref> He recorded his first career [[double (basketball)|double-double]] on December 12, 2017, with 10 points, 12 rebounds, and 6 assists in a 69–55 loss to [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Racers Can't Make Fast Start Last At Saint Louis |url=https://goracers.com/news/2017/12/12/mens-basketball-racers-at-slu.aspx |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=March 24, 2019 |date=December 12, 2017}}</ref> He posted his first triple-double on December 28, recording 11 points, 10 rebounds, and 14 assists in an 80–52 win over [[Eastern Illinois Panthers men's basketball|Eastern Illinois]]. It was the second triple-double in school history, the first coming from Isacc Miles in 1984, and was also the record for most assists at a [[CFSB Center]] game, surpassing the old mark of 12 established by [[Aubrey Reese]] against [[Alabama State Hornets basketball|Alabama State]] in 1999.<ref>''Murray State Basketball 2017-18 NCAA Tournament Guide'', p. 9.</ref> Morant also had the third-most assists in a single game by a Murray State player.<ref>{{cite web |title=Morant's Triple-Double Leads Racers Past EIU |url=https://goracers.com/news/2017/12/28/mens-basketball-morants-triple-double-leads-racers-past-eiu.aspx?path=mbball |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=December 26, 2018 |date=December 28, 2017}}</ref> On February 1, 2018, he scored a season-high 23 points against [[Southeast Missouri State Redhawks men's basketball|Southeast Missouri State]].<ref>{{cite web |title=55-Point Second Half Leads Racers To 4th Straight Win |url=https://goracers.com/news/2018/2/1/mens-basketball-55-point-second-half-leads-racers-to-4th-straight-win.aspx |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=December 26, 2018 |date=February 1, 2018}}</ref> After averaging 12.7 points, 6.5 rebounds, and 6.3 assists per game, Morant earned first-team All-OVC and OVC All-Newcomer Team accolades.<ref name="espnstats">{{cite web |title=Ja Morant Stats |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/stats/_/id/4279888/ja-morant |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=March 24, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Long |first1=James |title=Racers' Stark earns player of the year |url=http://www.kfvs12.com/story/37605414/mens-basketball-ovc-honors-racers-stark-earns-player-of-the-year/ |publisher=[[KFVS-TV]] |accessdate=December 26, 2018 |date=February 27, 2018}}</ref> He became the seventh freshman in 25 years to accumulate 150 assists, 150 rebounds, and 10 blocks while shooting at least 42 percent from the field.<ref name=hoy/>

=== Sophomore year ===
As a sophomore, Morant assumed a leading role for Murray State with the departures of key players [[Jonathan Stark (basketball)|Jonathan Stark]] and [[Terrell Miller (basketball)|Terrell Miller]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hickey |first1=Pat |title=Next task for the Aces? Figuring out how to defend future NBA lottery pick Ja Morant of Murray State |url=https://www.courierpress.com/story/sports/college/evansville/2018/12/17/evansville-basketball-next-path-ja-morant-and-murray-state/2339165002/ |website=[[Evansville Courier & Press]] |accessdate=December 26, 2018 |date=December 17, 2018}}</ref> In his season debut, he recorded 26 points and 11 assists in a 74–53 win against [[Wright State Raiders men's basketball|Wright State]].<ref name="item">{{cite web |last1=Winder |first1=Dave |title=Morant having impact at Murray State |url=https://www.theitem.com/stories/morant-having-impact-at-murray-state,318341 |website=[[The Item]] |accessdate=December 26, 2018 |date=November 16, 2018}}</ref> On November 24, 2018, Morant posted 29 points, a season-high 13 rebounds, and 12 assists in a 77–66 win over [[Missouri State Bears basketball|Missouri State]], becoming the first Murray State player to ever record multiple triple-doubles.<ref>{{cite web |title=Morant leads Murray State past Missouri State 77-66 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/11/24/morant-leads-murray-state-past-missouri-state-77-66/38600371/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=December 26, 2018 |date=November 24, 2018}}</ref> In his next game, he scored a season-high 38 points in a 78–72 loss to [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], the 12th-most single-game points by a player in school history.<ref>{{cite web |title=Showman Morant Dazzles But Racers Fall At Alabama |url=https://goracers.com/news/2018/11/26/mens-basketball-racers-at-alabama.aspx |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=December 26, 2018 |date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> By around December 2018, Morant was almost unanimously projected as a top-five selection in the [[2019 NBA draft]], and in late January 2019, at least one outlet forecasted him as the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall]] selection.<ref name=Forde>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/hungry-coach-led-discovery-viral-college-sensation-ja-morant-020738543.html |title=How a hungry coach led to the discovery of viral college sensation Ja Morant |first=Pat |last=Forde |publisher=Yahoo! Sports |date=January 29, 2019 |accessdate=January 30, 2019}}</ref> According to [[Yahoo! Sports]] journalist [[Pat Forde]], "He seems almost certain to be the first top-ten pick from a mid-major school in five years ([[Elfrid Payton (basketball)|Elfrid Payton]], [[Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns men's basketball|Louisiana-Lafayette]]), and could be the first true mid-major pick in the top five since [[Michael Olowokandi]] of [[Pacific Tigers men's basketball|Pacific]] went No. 1 in [[1998 NBA draft|1998]]."<ref name=Forde/>{{efn|Forde did not consider two top-five selections between 1998 and 2018 from schools outside the [[Power Five conferences|traditional power conferences]] to be "true mid-majors", saying "[[Lamar Odom]], the No. 4 pick in [[1999 NBA draft|1999]] out of [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]], really doesn't fit the mid-major profile. He was a hugely celebrated recruit who took a rather scandalous route to a second-tier program. Neither does [[Adam Morrison]], the No. 3 pick in [[2006 NBA draft|2006]] out of decided non-mid-major [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]]."<ref name=Forde/>}}

On January 10, 2019, Morant was named to the midseason top 25 watch list for the [[John R. Wooden Award]].<ref name="wooden">{{cite web |title=College basketball: 2019 John Wooden Award midseason top 25 announced |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2019-01-09/2019-john-wooden-award-midseason-top-25-announced |publisher=[[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] |accessdate=January 30, 2019 |date=January 10, 2019}}</ref> On the same day, he broke the school record for most assists in a single game, with 18, while scoring 26 points against [[UT Martin Skyhawks men's basketball|UT Martin]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Morant & Brown Lead Racers' Blitz At UTM |url=https://goracers.com/news/2019/1/10/mens-basketball-morant-brown-lead-racers-blitz-at-utm.aspx |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=March 10, 2019 |date=January 10, 2019}}</ref> He established a new scoring career-high nine days later on January 19, when he recorded 40 points, 11 assists, and 5 [[steal (basketball)|steals]], shooting 21-of-21 from the [[free throw]] line, in a victory over [[SIU Edwardsville Cougars men's basketball|SIU Edwardsville]].<ref name="siue">{{cite web |title=Ja Morant Scores 40, Murray State Rolls Past SIU-Edwardsville |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/01/19/ja-morant-scores-40-points-murray-state-win |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=January 20, 2019 |date=January 19, 2019}}</ref> He broke the OVC record for most consecutive free throws made in a game, and he became the tenth player in Murray State history to record a 40-point game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Morant Sets OVC Free Throw Record - Racers Win At SIUE |url=https://goracers.com/news/2019/1/19/mens-basketball-morant-sets-ovc-free-throw-record-racers-win-at-siue.aspx |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=January 20, 2019 |date=January 19, 2019}}</ref> Morant also became the first [[NCAA Division I]] men's player in 20 years to tally at least 40 points, 10 assists, and 5 steals in a single game.<ref name=siue/> On February 2, Morant collected 28 points and 7 assists in a 67–63 win over [[Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles men's basketball|Tennessee Tech]]. He broke the school single-season assist record of 212 set by Chad Townsend in the 1996–97 season.<ref name="assistrecord">{{cite web |title=Racers Rally For Win At Tech - Morant Sets Assist Record |url=https://goracers.com/news/2019/2/2/mens-basketball-racer-men-at-ttu.aspx |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=March 10, 2019 |date=February 2, 2019}}</ref> After posting 25 points, 8 rebounds, and 14 assists in a 102–70 victory over [[Eastern Kentucky Colonels men's basketball|Eastern Kentucky]], Morant became the 46th Murray State player with 1,000 career points and eclipsed the OVC record for single-season assists previously held for 32 years by [[Duane Washington]] of [[Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders men's basketball|Middle Tennessee]].<ref name="century">{{cite web |title=Racers Hit Century Mark - Morant Sets OVC Assist Record & Reaches 1,000 Points |url=https://goracers.com/news/2019/2/16/mens-basketball-racers-hit-century-mark-morant-sets-ovc-record-reaches-1-000-points.aspx |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=March 10, 2019 |date=February 16, 2019}}</ref>

At the end of the regular season, he was named [[Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|OVC Player of the Year]] and first-team All-OVC, while [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball season assists leaders|leading the NCAA Division I in assists]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Racer Trio Named All-OVC - Morant MVP & Buchanan Defensive POY |url=https://goracers.com/news/2019/3/4/mens-basketball-all-ovc-men-awards.aspx |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=March 10, 2019 |date=March 5, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Northam |first1=Mitchell |title=3 one-on-one matchups we can’t wait to see in the NCAA tournament |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/2019-03-18/3-one-one-matchups-we-cant-wait-see-ncaa-tournament |publisher=[[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] |accessdate=March 24, 2019 |date=March 20, 2019}}</ref> He later earned first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors from the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] and second-team All-American honors from ''[[Sporting News]]''.<ref name="usbwa">{{cite web |title=2018-19 Men's All-America Team |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2019/allamerica190318.html |publisher=[[United States Basketball Writers Association]] |accessdate=March 24, 2019 |date=March 18, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Morant Named Second-Team All-American by Sporting News |url=http://www.ovcsports.com/news/2019/3/11/mens-basketball-morant-named-second-team-all-american-by-sporting-news.aspx |publisher=[[Ohio Valley Conference]] |accessdate=March 24, 2019 |date=March 11, 2019}}</ref> On March 8, in the semifinals of the [[2019 Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|OVC Tournament]] versus [[Jacksonville State Gamecocks men's basketball|Jacksonville State]], Morant scored 29 points, including a game-winning [[three-point play]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Morant hits winner, sends Murray St. to OVC final |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401121716 |website=''[[ESPN]]'' |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=March 10, 2019 |date=March 9, 2019}}</ref> One day later, he recorded 36 points, 7 rebounds, and 3 assists in a 77–65 victory over [[Belmont Bruins men's basketball|Belmont]] for the OVC Tournament title.<ref name="he">{{cite web |last1=He |first1=Eric |title=Ja Morant drops 36 points against Belmont as Murray State punches ticket to March Madness |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ja-morant-murray-state-punch-their-ticket-to-ncaa-tournament-031640957.html |publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]] |accessdate=March 10, 2019 |date=March 9, 2019}}</ref> Morant was subsequently named the tournament's MVP.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wimsatt |first1=Jessica |title=Murray State's Ja Morant rising to stardom |url=https://www.tristatehomepage.com/news/local-news/murray-state-s-ja-morant-rising-to-stardom/1838185894 |publisher=[[WEHT]] |accessdate=March 10, 2019 |date=March 9, 2019}}</ref> On March 21, in an 83–64 win over fifth-seeded [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] in the first round of the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2019 NCAA Tournament]], Morant posted 17 points, 11 rebounds, and 16 assists. He became the eighth player to officially record a triple-double in the history of the tournament.<ref name="marquette">{{cite web |title=Morant Thrives, Racers Advance With NCAA Win Over Marquette |url=https://goracers.com/news/2019/3/21/mens-basketball-morant-thrives-racers-advance-with-ncaa-win-over-marquette.aspx |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=March 24, 2019 |date=March 21, 2019}}</ref>{{efn|The NCAA's official Division I record book only recognizes triple-doubles that took place in seasons in which the NCAA kept track of the relevant statistical categories throughout Division I. Assists were recorded in the 1950–51 and 1951–52 seasons, but were not recorded again until 1983–84. Blocked shots and steals were first officially kept in 1985–86. Some listings of tournament triple-doubles include games that took place in tournaments in which the official scorers kept count of all relevant statistics, but the NCAA did not.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/m_basketball_RB/2019/D1.pdf |title=Individual Records |work=2018–19 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Records |page=2 |accessdate=March 23, 2019}}</ref>}} In the second round, he chipped in 28 points in a season-ending 90–62 loss to fourth-seeded [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]]. During the game, Morant set school records for career assists and single-season points.<ref name="fsu">{{cite web |title=Racers' NCAA Run Ends With Loss To Florida State |url=https://goracers.com/news/2019/3/23/mens-basketball-racers-ncaa-run-ends-with-loss-to-florida-state.aspx |publisher=Murray State University Athletics |accessdate=March 24, 2019 |date=March 23, 2019}}</ref>
He closed his sophomore campaign averaging 24.5 points, 5.7 rebounds, 10 assists, and 1.8 steals per game.<ref name=espnstats/> Morant became the first NCAA player to ever average at least 20 points and 10 assists per game in a single season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=West |first1=Jenna |title=Ja Morant Ends Season as First Player in NCAA History to Average 20 Points, 10 Assists |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/03/23/ja-morant-points-assists-game-record-ncaa-history-murray-state |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=March 24, 2019 |date=March 23, 2019}}</ref> 

Following Murray State's loss in the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2019 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament]], Morant announced his intention to forgo his final two seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA draft]], where he is projected to be a first-round selection.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26432657|title=Murray State star Morant declares for NBA draft|work=[[ESPN]]|date=April 3, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Morant has a younger sister, Teniya, who grew up playing basketball with him in their backyard and now competes for Hillcrest Middle School in Dalzell.<ref name=Woo/><ref>{{cite web |title=Lady Barons first in shooting qualifier |url=https://www.theitem.com/stories/lady-barons-first-in-shooting-qualifier,319566 |website=[[The Item]] |accessdate=January 30, 2019 |date=December 12, 2018}}</ref> He has the words "beneath no one," advice his mother gave him, tattooed to his left arm.<ref name=Woo/>
